newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee higher, output hinges on weather.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee higher, output hinges on weather.

text.p: Indonesian coffee prices were higher on Monday from a week ago due to tight supply, with traders saying that production next year could be hit if a drought sweeping across the archipelago is prolonged.
They said the flowering process had begun in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, but added that the area had been parched by two months of dry weather.

"I surveyed some growing areas in Lampung recently and found that the leaves in lowland trees had turned yellowish because of a lack of rain," one trader said. "If the dry weather continues, I think the production will be affected next year."
He said that flowering in the region's highlands were, however, proceeding well.

"It now all depends on the weather. If the rains come on time, we might see a 10-percent increase in production next year. If not, there might be a 10-percent decline," he said. "At this moment, it's still 50-50 either way."
Traders said it was still too early in the year to predict a crop size for 1998, adding that it was now acknowledged by the trade that output this year would be sharply lower.
Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, said in June that 1997 production was expected to plunge by 160,000 tonnes to 290,000 tonnes from 1996.
Traders said much of the beans available for exports would run out by September, adding that the next harvest was expected begin only in March or April.
"The market is very quiet, with supply remaining tight," one trader said. "Prices are still high and except for bits and pieces, there's not much export business."
"Players are also looking at the possible size of the next crop due to the dry season, but it is still too early to make any forecast about 1998 output," he added.

He said players were also keeping an eye on the weather situation in top producer Brazil. Weather forecasts citing a slight possibility of a freeze in Brazil provided some underlying support to New York coffee prices last Friday.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corporation, however, said on Monday there were no damaging cold in sight for Brazil's coffee areas over the next five days.

Indonesian grade four robusta coffee prices were quoted at 3,700-3,800 rupiah/kg in Lampung, compared with 3,500-3,600 rupiah a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,550-$1,575 a tonne, against $1,550 fob Lampung.
